To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

methanol molecules react on stoichiometric or O-rich RuO surfaces to form adsorbed CHxOy species, and that CH2OH2 and CH2O2 are the main intermediates for complete and partial oxidation, respectively.

(1) CH3OH adsorption is highly favored on O-rich RuO 2(110) relative to stoichiometric Ru O2(110) and (2) complete oxidation of metha nol is strongly preferred on RuO 2 surfaces with low O-atom coverage and becomes increasingly favored with increas ing CH3OH coverage on stoichiometric surfaces and with increasing coverage of O-atoms adsorbed on top of Ru sites on O-rich Ru O2 surfaces.

methanol molecules react with bridging and on-top O-atom sites on the RuO2(100) surface to form adsorbed CHxOy species, which desorb as CHxOH (CH3OH, CH3O, CH2O, and CH3OH) or evolve to CHxOyOz species (CH2O2, CH2OO, and CH3O2).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental mechanisms of methanol oxidation on RuO2 and the influence of O-rich surface domains on selectivity toward complete oxidation.
the adsorption and reactivity of small organic molecules on metal oxide surfaces.
elucidating the role of surface oxygen atoms in the oxidation of methanol to formaldehyde and carbon dioxide on RuO2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the complete oxidation is favored on stoichiometric surfaces at low coverages, while the partial oxidation is favored on oxygen-rich surfaces at higher coverages, and that both processes are facilitated by the presence of O-atoms on the RuO2(1 1 0) surface.

methanol oxidation on stoichometric and oxygen rich RuO2(100) proceeds through a common mechanism, with the only significant difference being the relative rates at which CH3OH is dehydrogenated to CH2O, and the relative rates at CH3O is hydrogenated to CH3OH, on the two surface types.

methanol oxidation on stoichometric and O-rich surfaces proceeds via a similar mechanism but that the rate-limiting step is the formation of the CH2O2 intermediate, which becomes limited by the number of O-atoms on the stoichometric surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

RuO2 catalysts are highly active and selective for the complete oxidation of alcohols and that the activity of the catalyst is determined by the density of active O-atoms and the presence of adsorbed O-rich domains.

the complete oxidation is preferred for CH3OH adsorption on both stoichiometric and highly O-rich RuO 2(110) but that the selectivity toward the full oxidation increases with the increasing O coverage on RuO2 surface.
the selectivity of methanol oxidation on RuO2 depends on the initial coverage of methanol and on the coverage of on-top oxygen (Oot).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activity and selectivity of RuO2(100) surfaces toward the oxidation of methanol can be tuned by varying the coverage of on-top (bridging) oxygen atoms.
the oxidation state of RuO2(111) surfaces can be used to tailor their reactivity toward the complete oxidation and/or partial oxidation of CH3O species.

RuO2(1 1 0) is an excellent catalyst for methanol oxidation at high-temperature, and that the activity of RuO2(1110) for complete oxidation of CH 3OH is significantly higher than for the partial oxidation to CH 2 O.
